facts.statement: The genus Bellubrunnus was first described and named in 2012 by David W. E. Hone, Helmut Tischlinger, Eberhard Frey, and Martin Röper.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus was first described and named by David W. E. Hone, Helmut Tischlinger, Eberhard Frey and Martin Röper in 2012

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the summer of 2002 by a team led by Monika Rothgaenger, after whom the species is named.
facts.quote: It was found in the summer of 2002 by an excavation team led by Monika Rothgaenger, the namesake of the species.

facts.statement: Bellubrunnus lived during the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage) in southern Germany.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus (meaning "the beautiful one of Brunn" in Latin) is an extinct genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage) of southern Germany.

facts.statement: The genus Bellubrunnus contains only one known species, Bellubrunnus rothgaengeri.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Bellubrunnus rothgaengeri.

facts.statement: Bellubrunnus is distinguished by lacking long tail vertebrae projections, having fewer jaw teeth, and possessing wingtips that curve forward instead of backward.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus is distinguished from other rhamphorhynchids by its lack of long projections on the vertebrae of the tail, fewer teeth in the jaws, and wingtips that curve forward rather than sweep backward as in other pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in a quarry at Kohlstatt near Brunn, in rock layers beneath the Solnhofen Limestone.
facts.quote: It comes from a quarry at Kohlstatt near the village of Brunn, Upper Palatinate, in a layer of rock that underlies the better-known Solnhofen Limestone.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to approximately 151 million years ago, during the late Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The quarry dates to the late Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic period, about 151 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype represents one of the smallest known pterosaur fossils, with a wingspan of less than one foot.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Bellubrunnus represents a small individual, with a wingspan of less than a foot, and is one of the smallest pterosaur fossils known.

facts.statement: Twenty-one small teeth are preserved in the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: Twenty-one small teeth are preserved splaying out from the jaws.

facts.statement: The eyes are exceptionally large, occupying about one-third of the skull's total length.
facts.quote: The eyes are very large relative to the size of the skull, occupying around a third of its total length.

facts.statement: Features such as a shortened skull, large eyes, unfused skull bones, and poorly ossified limbs suggest the specimen was an immature individual when it died.
facts.quote: Both a shortened skull and large eyes are considered characteristics of juvenile pterosaurs, and other features, such as unfused skull bones and poorly ossified limb bones, suggest that BSP–1993–XVIII–2 was an immature individual when it died.

facts.statement: The humerus is exceptionally long compared to the femur, with a length ratio of 1.4, a unique trait distinguishing it from other rhamphorhynchids.
facts.quote: The great length of the humerus in comparison to the length of the femur ("fe") or upper leg bone, with a ratio of 1.4, distinguishes it from other rhamphorhynchids and is a second autapomorphy.

facts.statement: The femur lacks a neck between the head and shaft, a unique characteristic of Bellubrunnus.
facts.quote: A fourth autapomorphy is that the thighbone lacks a "neck" between its head and the shaft.

facts.statement: Short chevrons and zygapophyses on the tail vertebrae indicate that Bellubrunnus had a relatively flexible tail.
facts.quote: Another distinguishing feature of Bellubrunnus is the shortness of its chevrons and zygapophyses on the caudal or tail vertebrae ("cdv"), indicating the tail was relatively flexible.

facts.statement: The forward-curving wingtips may have improved maneuverability by increasing air resistance and turbulence, though their exact function remains unknown.
facts.quote: Although their exact function is unknown, curved wingtips, inducing instability by increased air resistance and turbulence, may have allowed Bellubrunnus to maneuver itself better in the air.

facts.statement: The curved wingtips may have helped stabilize the wing membrane flaps, which were prone to fluttering in other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: They also may, in combination with a different orientation of the actinofibrils of the wing membrane, have stabilized the soft tissue flaps at the ends of the wings, which were expanded in most pterosaurs and may have been prone to fluttering.

facts.statement: Bellubrunnus is classified within the family Rhamphorhynchidae and the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus was assigned to the Rhamphorhynchidae and more precisely to the Rhamphorhynchinae.

facts.statement: The Brunn limestones, where Bellubrunnus was found, were likely deposited in lagoons and reefs of an island region.
facts.quote: Like the Solnhofen, the Brunn limestones were likely laid down in the lagoons and reefs of an island region.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Bellubrunnus was a fish-eater and possibly the direct evolutionary ancestor of Rhamphorhynchus, though this relationship requires more fossil evidence to confirm.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus may have occupied the same ecological niche as Rhamphorhynchus, that of a piscivore or fish-eater, and may even have been its direct evolutionary ancestor, forming a chronogenus relation within a single persisting population, although more fossils are needed to confirm this relationship.

facts.statement: O'Sullivan and Martill (2015) argued that many distinguishing features of Bellubrunnus are problematic due to a lack of ontogenetic studies, leaving it uncertain whether it is a distinct genus or merely a juvenile form of Rhamphorhynchus.
facts.quote: O'Sullivan and Martill (2015) found the majority of the purported distinguishing characters of Bellubrunnus to be problematic, stressing especially the lack of in-depth studies into the way rhamphorhynchid skeletons changed through ontogeny; this means that it remains uncertain whether the differences between Bellubrunnus and Rhamphorhynchus do indeed confirm that they are distinct taxa or whether these differences are merely ontogenetic in nature.

facts.statement: Despite similarities, O'Sullivan and Martill noted that the lack of elongate tail supports and the forward-curving fourth wing phalanx suggest Bellubrunnus may not be the same species as Rhamphorhynchus muensteri.
facts.quote: The authors, however, noted that two characters of the species Bellubrunnus rothgaengeri (the lack of elongate caudal supports on the vertebrae and the anteriorly curving wing phalanx IV) make it possible that it is not conspecific with Rhamphorhynchus muensteri.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Bellubrunnus is a single complete and articulated skeleton cataloged as BSP–1993–XVIII–2.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus es conocido a partir de un único esqueleto completo y articulado conocido como BSP–1993–XVIII–2.

facts.statement: The species name rothgaengeri honors Monika Rothgaenger, who led the excavation team that found the holotype in 2002.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en 2002 por un equipo de excavación liderado por Monika Rothgaenger, de cuyo apellido deriva el nombre de la especie.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in a quarry near the village of Brunn in Upper Palatinate, in a rock layer beneath the famous Solnhofen Limestone.
facts.quote: Proviene de una cantera cercana al pueblo de Brunn, Alto Palatinado, en una capa de roca que subyace a la mejor conocida Caliza de Solnhofen.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: La cantera data del Kimmeridgiense en el período Jurásico Superior, hace entre 155-150 millones de años.

facts.statement: The genus Bellubrunnus was described and named by David W. E. Hone, Helmut Tischlinger, Eberhard Frey, and Martin Röper in 2012.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus fue descrito y nombrado por David W. E. Hone, Helmut Tischlinger, Eberhard Frey y Martin Röper en 2012

facts.statement: Bellubrunnus is distinguished from other rhamphorhynchids by lacking long projections on tail vertebrae, having few teeth in the jaws, and having wing tips that curve forward rather than backward.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus se distingue de otros ranforrínquidos por su carencia de largas proyecciones en las vértebras de la cola, tener pocos dientes en las mandíbulas y puntas de las alas que se curvan hacia adelante más que inclinarse hacia atrás como en muchos otros pterosaurios.

facts.statement: The eyes were very large relative to the skull size, occupying nearly one-third of its total length.
facts.quote: Los ojos son muy grandes para el tamaño del cráneo, ocupando cerca de un tercio de su longitud total.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the short skull and large eyes indicate the specimen was an immature individual when it died, supported by unfused skull bones and poorly ossified limb bones.
facts.quote: Se considera que tanto el cráneo corto como los grandes ojos son características de los pterosaurios juveniles, así como otros rasgos, como los huesos sin fusionar del cráneo y los huesos de las extremidades apenas osificados, lo que sugiere que BSP–1993–XVIII–2 era un individuo inmaduro cuando murió.

facts.statement: The unfused scapulocoracoid bone suggests the individual may have been less than one year old.
facts.quote: El hueso escapulocoracoides sin fusionar en la cintura escapular sugiere que pudo haber tenido menos de un año de vida.

facts.statement: The distal phalanx supporting the wing tip in the specimen curves forward.
facts.quote: El último hueso del dedo o falange distal que mantenía el ala se curva hacia adelante.

facts.statement: Although its exact function is unknown, researchers suggest the forward-curving wing tips may have allowed Bellubrunnus to maneuver better in the air.
facts.quote: Aunque su función exacta es desconocida, las puntas de alas curvadas pueden haberle permitido a Bellubrunnus maniobrar mejor en el aire.

facts.statement: The Brunn limestone was likely deposited in the bottoms of lagoons and reefs in an island region, similar to the Solnhofen environment.
facts.quote: Como en Solnhofen, las calizas de Brunn fueron probablemente depositadas en el fondo de lagunas y arrecifes en una región de islas.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Bellubrunnus occupied the same ecological niche as Rhamphorhynchus and was its direct evolutionary ancestor, though more fossils are needed to confirm this relationship.
facts.quote: Bellubrunnus puede haber ocupado el mismo nicho ecológico de Rhamphorhynchus, y puede incluso haber sido su ancestro evolutivo directo, aunque se necesitan más fósiles para confirmar esa relación.
